title: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English (0500)

officialDocument.title: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029
officialDocument.publisher: Cambridge University Press & Assessment (Cambridge International Education)

sourceNote: The syllabus describes its content as skills under Reading, Writing and Speaking and Listening rather than numbered topics. The three topics follow those headings; the sub-topics group the listed skills and the paper tasks in section 4 (Details of the assessment). Topic codes and objective codes are ours; references such as (R1) and (W3) name the syllabus's assessment objectives. Objective statements are our own paraphrase.
notes: Assessment overview as read (2027-2029 syllabus): all candidates take Paper 1 Reading (2 hours, 80 marks, 50%: Question 1 comprehension of Text A, 20 marks; Question 2 summary of Text B, 2(a) a selective summary of no more than 120 words and 2(b) a short answer on attitudes and opinions, 20 marks; Question 3 short-answer questions and a language task of about 200-250 words on Text C, 20 marks; Question 4 an extended response to Text C of about 250-300 words as a letter, report, journal, speech, interview or article, 20 marks) and either Paper 2 Directed Writing and Composition (2 hours, 80 marks, 50%: Section A directed writing based on one or two texts of 550-650 words, 1(a) 5 marks and 1(b) a 250-350 word speech, letter, article or report, 35 marks; Section B one composition of about 350-450 words from four titles, two descriptive and two narrative, 40 marks) or Component 3 Coursework Portfolio (80 marks, 50%, three assignments). Component 4 Speaking and Listening (about 10-12 minutes, 40 marks) is optional and separately endorsed.

This version is examined from 2027. A student sitting the examination in 2026 is examined on the 2024-2026 syllabus, which is not in the repository; the 2027-2029 version is published as the current version because new students now will sit 2027 or later. Check the 2027-2029 changes listed in the syllabus (the Paper 1 marking criteria and Paper 2 Question 1(b) reading marks changed).
The platform cannot run the coursework portfolio or the speaking and listening test; lessons and practice cover the skills they assess, and the mocks simulate Papers 1 and 2 only.

components.name: Paper 1: Reading
components.description: Four compulsory questions on three reading texts (about 1400 words in total): comprehension, summary, short answers and a language task, and an extended response.

components.name: Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition
components.description: Section A: directed writing based on one or two texts (40 marks). Section B: one descriptive or narrative composition from a choice of four titles (40 marks).

components.name: Component 3: Coursework Portfolio
components.description: Alternative to Paper 2: three extended writing assignments, internally assessed and externally moderated.

components.name: Component 4: Speaking and Listening Test
components.description: Optional: an individual talk and a conversation, separately endorsed (grades 1 to 5).

topics.name: Reading
topics.description: AO1 Reading: tested in Paper 1 (80% of its marks) and in Paper 2 Section A and Component 3 (20%). Texts from the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, fiction and non-fiction, including discursive essays, reviews and articles.

objectives.text: Show understanding of what a text states explicitly, and of the words and phrases within it (R1).
Show understanding of implicit meanings and attitudes (R2).
Explain ideas from a text in their own words.

children.name: Analysing and evaluating facts, ideas and opinions

objectives.text: Analyse, evaluate and develop facts, ideas and opinions, supporting points with evidence from the text (R3).
Recognise how writers influence readers through facts, ideas, perspectives, opinions and bias.
Show understanding of how writers achieve effects and influence readers (R4).
Recognise and respond to linguistic devices, figurative language and imagery, explaining the effect of chosen words and phrases.
Select and use information for a specific purpose (R5).
Write a selective summary in continuous prose and in their own words, within a word limit.
Use, develop and interpret ideas from a text in an extended response written in role as a letter, report, journal, speech, interview or article.
Read a range of literary and non-literary texts and discuss characters, setting, plot, themes and style.

topics.name: Writing
topics.description: AO2 Writing: tested in Paper 2 or Component 3 (80% of their marks) and in Paper 1 (20%). Descriptive, narrative, discursive, argumentative and persuasive writing; letters, reports, articles, journals, speeches, interviews and summaries.

objectives.text: Use, develop and evaluate information from one or two texts to write a discursive, argumentative or persuasive speech, letter, article or report.
Organise and structure facts, ideas and opinions for deliberate effect (W2).

children.name: Letters, reports, articles, speeches, journals and interviews

objectives.text: Write in the conventions of letters, reports, articles, speeches, journals and interviews for a given audience and purpose.
Express what is thought, felt and imagined in descriptive compositions (W1).
Write narrative compositions that are well structured and engage the reader.
Write discursive, argumentative and persuasive texts that develop a line of reasoning.
Use language appropriate to purpose and engage the audience (W4).
Plan and paragraph writing so that it is coherent and well organised.
Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures appropriate to the context (W3).
Make accurate use of spelling, punctuation and grammar (W5).

topics.name: Speaking and listening
topics.description: AO3 Speaking and Listening: the optional Component 4 test (individual talk and conversation), separately endorsed with grades 1 to 5.

objectives.text: Articulate experience and present facts, ideas and opinions for deliberate effect in a prepared talk (SL1, SL2).
Communicate clearly, purposefully and fluently in a register appropriate to the context (SL3, SL4).
Listen and respond appropriately in conversation, developing ideas and responding to questions and prompts (SL5).
